author: Katarina Hoije
description: Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye dissolved the government and dismissed Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko, increasing the risk of political unrest after months of simmering tensions between the two leaders.
title: Senegal’s Faye Sacks Sonko Government Amid Widening Policy Rift

author: Jamie Tarabay
description: Aaron Lukas, the former CIA officer selected to replace Tulsi Gabbard as spy chief, aligns with some of President Donald Trump’s most ardent beliefs, including that intelligence agencies have become infected with wokeness, and that allegations of a Russian operation to sway the 2016 election are a hoax.
title: Ex-CIA Officer Tapped to Replace Gabbard Blasted ‘Toxic’ DEI Culture

description: Former Fed Governor Betsy Duke discusses the swearing in of new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh. She says that both Kevin Warsh and former Fed Chair Jerome Powell are both natural leaders. She discusses the outlook of the Fed going forward with its new chairman. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on “The Close.” (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fmr. Fed Governor Says Warsh, Powell Both Natural Leaders

author: Maggie Eastland, Tyler Kendall
description: The Trump administration continues to weigh US tariffs on imported semiconductors to boost domestic chip manufacturing, though there are no immediate plans to impose any new levies, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said.
title: US Weighs Chip Tariffs to Spur Domestic Growth, Trade Chief Says

description: President Donald Trump says Democratic policies on crime and taxes were leading to an exodus of businesses and taxpayers from the nation’s financial capital. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Accuses Democratic Policies of Driving Companies Out of NYC

author: Emily Forgash, Jennifer A Dlouhy, Mark Chediak
description: About $50 billion in wind investments and 150,000 jobs are imperiled by the Trump administration’s effective halt to approvals for new onshore projects, a trade group said.
title: Wind-Permit Stall Is Threatening $50 Billion in US Developments

description: Bloomberg's Mike McKee and Stuart Paul discuss the future of the Federal Reserve under Kevin Warsh after he was sworn in as the new fed chair. Then, Qualcomm's head of Automotive, Robotics and IoT Businesses Nakul Duggal talks the semiconductor company's new deal with Stellantis to advance vehicle tech as the self-driving landscape grows across the automotive industry. Plus, President and CEO of Stew Leonard's grocery stores Stew Leonard Jr., breaks down the cost of a memorial day cookout as concerns about food and fuel prices squeeze consumers. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Kevin Warsh Sworn In As New Fed Chair| Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 5/22/2026

author: Nathan R Dean
description: Next steps with Iran and the central bank’s independence were front and center.
title: What Europe Wants to Know About Trump, the War and the Fed

author: Kate Sullivan
description: President Donald Trump assailed Democrats over crime levels in blue jurisdictions as he sought to boost one of the Republican Party’s most vulnerable lawmakers during a campaign stop in New York.
title: Trump Hits Democrats on Crime, Taxes to Boost NY’s Lawler

author: Patricia Hurtado, Zoe Tillman
description: A federal judge in Tennessee dismissed the human-smuggling case against Kilmar Armando Abrego Garcia, a Salvadoran migrant, after concluding the government had brought the case as retaliation for his legal fight against being deported.
title: Abrego Garcia Human-Smuggling Case Dismissed by Tennessee Judge

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Joe Mathieu discusses Kevin Warsh's swearing-in as the next Chair of the Federal Reserve. On today's show, Kpler Head of Policy and Geopolitical Risk Michelle Brouhard, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino, Friday Reporter Public Affairs Founder Lisa Camooso Miller, Goldman Sachs Vice Chairman Rob Kaplan and Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Warsh Sworn In As Fed Chair | Balance of Power: Early Edition 5/22/2026

author: Patricia Hurtado
description: A Columbia University graduate student detained by US authorities over his role in pro-Palestinian protests will ask the US Supreme Court to halt his deportation after a federal appeals court rejected his request for a re-hearing.
title: Ex-Columbia Student to Ask Supreme Court to Stop Deportation

description: Sanjay Mehrotra, President, Chairman and CEO of Micron joined Bloomberg's Tyler Kendall to discuss the company's significant expansion of DRAM manufacturing in the US. He also discussed the demand for AI, and how he sees memory chip shortage lasting beyond 2026.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Micron CEO Sees Memory Chip Shortage Lasting Beyond 2026

author: Andrew Rosati
description: President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is leading Brazil’s presidential election as Senator Flavio Bolsonaro suffers from his ties to the man at the center of a massive banking scandal, a new poll showed.
title: Bolsonaro Falls Behind Lula After Link to Scandal-Plagued Banker

description: Goldman Sachs Vice Chairman Rob Kaplan, a former Dallas Fed president, spoke with Julie Fine after Kevin Warsh was sworn in as Fed Chair. Kaplan said he expects newly sworn-in Fed Chair Kevin Warsh will be independent from political influence, which is essential for the central bank to maintain credibility  with the public and markets. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Tells Warsh to Do ‘Own Thing’ as Fed Chair Sworn In

description: The United Arab Emirates has made a more concerted push for an end to the Iran war in recent days, joining Saudi Arabia and Qatar in urging US President Donald Trump to give negotiations a chance, according to several people familiar with the matter. Michelle Brouhard, Head of Policy and Geopolitical Risk at Kpler joins Balance of Power to discuss.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: UAE Joins Saudis, Qatar in Urging Trump Not to Restart War

author: Gerry Doyle
description: A top Pentagon official’s remarks that the US had halted arms sales to Taiwan to ensure sufficient munitions for the Iran war are the latest sign that the conflict has sapped American military readiness, including for a potential confrontation with China.
title: US Faces Lower Arsenal, Extended Deployments After Months of Iran Fighting

author: Alicia A. Caldwell
description: Foreigners applying for permanent residency in the US will now have to go back to their home countries to seek green cards.
title: Trump to Force Foreigners Seeking Green Cards to Go Home First

author: Mathieu Dion
description: Canada is dealing with active separatist movements in two of its largest provinces, sparking wariness among bondholders in the US, according to Quebec’s finance minister.
title: Debt Investors Press Quebec Finance Minister on Separatism in Canada

author: Bob Van Voris
description: BNP Paribas SA asked a federal appeals court to reverse a verdict of nearly $21 million against the bank over allegations that it funded a regime in Sudan that committed widespread human rights abuses.
title: BNP Paribas Asks Appeals Court to Toss $21 Million Sudan Verdict

author: Sanne Wass, Frances Schwartzkopff
description: The leader of Denmark’s Liberal Party failed to form a government in record-long coalition talks, potentially handing caretaker Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen a renewed chance to secure a third term in office.
title: Denmark Government Talks Stall, Improving Frederiksen’s Odds

author: Suzanne Lynch
description: Ireland is seeking to join the next phase of the EU’s flagship defense program as the country steps up spending on security and defense.
title: Ireland Aims to Join Next Phase of Flagship EU Defense Loan Fund

author: Natalia Drozdiak
description: Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard, whose anti-war views had spurred tension with the White House, said she was resigning from her post to help her husband confront a bone-cancer diagnosis.
title: Gabbard to Resign as Intelligence Director After Awkward Tenure

description: Kevin Warsh says he'll lead a "reform-oriented" Federal Reserve and goals will be pursued with "independence and resolve." In the months leading up to his nomination, Warsh said the Fed was not lowering rates enough. He speaks during the ceremony at the White House.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Warsh Says He'll Lead a 'Reform-Oriented' Fed

author: Eyk Henning, Michael Nienaber
description: Germany is balking at terms for taking a proposed 40% stake in tank maker KNDS NV, in a bid to limit how much the government pays for its share, people familiar with the matter said.
title: German Government Balking at Price for Pre-IPO Stake in Tankmaker KNDS

description: Kevin Warsh was sworn into office as the 17th chair of the Fed, promising the biggest shakeup in decades at the US central bank, and takes over at a tense moment for the economy and the central bank. Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas administered the oath at the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Kevin Warsh Sworn In as 17th Federal Reserve Chair

author: MacOn Atkinson
description: Democrats on the Senate Finance Committee called on chairman Mike Crapo (R-Idaho) Friday to launch a bipartisan probe into the Justice Department’s new fund for victims of government weaponization.
title: Wyden, Finance Panel Democrats Seek Investigation of DOJ Fund

description: President Donald Trump says no one in the US is better prepared to lead the Federal Reserve than Kevin Warsh as he swears Warsh in at the White House as the 17th chair of the Fed. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Tells Warsh to 'Do Your Own Thing' at Fed

description:
A Turkish court decision to remove the leadership of the country’s main opposition party caused the main index to tumble to its lowest in six weeks, then reverse losses within the day.

Murat Oztaskin explains what this could mean for markets and longtime president, Recep Tayyip Erdogan. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: What Turkey’s PoliticalDrama Means forErdogan and Markets

author: Amanda L. Gordon
description: Ken Griffin, one of the biggest political donors in recent election cycles, has made his first federal contribution for the 2026 midterm races.
title: Ken Griffin Gives $5 Million to GOP in First Midterm Donation

author: Paul Vecchiatto
description: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa’s legal team plans to file court papers early next week seeking a review of an independent panel’s report that found he may have breached the constitution in his handling of a burglary at his game farm.
title: South Africa President to Appeal Against Farm Cash Report Monday

author: Anthony Halpin
description: President Vladimir Putin ordered defense officials to prepare what he said were options for retaliation after he accused Ukraine of attacking a college in the Russian-occupied Luhansk region, killing at least six people.
title: Putin Vows Response After Saying Six Died in College Strike

author: Jan Bratanic
description: Slovenian lawmakers elected nationalist leader Janez Jansa as the country’s next premier, tilting another European Union member to the right and handing Donald Trump a potential ally in the bloc.
title: Trump Gets Another Ally in EU With Jansa’s Return in Slovenia

author: Meg Short
description: The Financial Conduct Authority is considering implementing a quarterly disclosure regime for private credit firms operating in the UK, requiring them to disclose portfolios, valuations and terms.
title: UK’s FCA Weighs Compulsory Disclosure for Private Credit Firms

author: Jorge Valero
description: The European Union’s industry chief said that businesses on the continent haven’t done enough to reduce major dependencies on China.
title: EU Warns Companies to Diversify Supply Lines From China Faster

description: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller now says he can't rule out voting to raise interest rates if inflation doesn’t start to slow soon, saying “inflation is not headed in the right direction." Waller made the comments during a speech in Germany. Bloomberg's Michael McKee reports.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fed's Waller Now Says Rate Increases Are Possible

author: Kate Duffy
description: The Royal International Air Tattoo at RAF Fairford, the UK’s biggest military air show, has been canceled this summer because US aircraft are using the venue for missions related to the Iran war, which continues to have wide-ranging impacts.
title: UK Military Air Show Canceled Over Middle East War Uncertainty

author: Beril Akman, Kerim Karakaya
description: With a packed schedule of meetings and speeches in front of London investors, Turkey’s top economic officials set out on Thursday to ease concerns about the country’s accelerating pace of inflation.
title: Turkey’s London Investor Pitch Gets Upended by Markets Tailspin

author: Chris Strohm, Lydia Beyoud
description: The House Oversight Committee is investigating how customers of Kalshi and Polymarket could be using non-public information to engage in insider trading, escalating concerns about prediction markets after some suspiciously well timed trades.
title: House Panel to Investigate Insider Trading on Prediction Markets

author: David Herbling
description: Kenyans should brace themselves for tougher economic times ahead because of the fallout from the Iran war, Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi said.
title: Kenyan Premier Warns of Tougher Economic Times Ahead on Iran War

author: Bastian Benrath-Wright
description: Switzerland is adopting most of the European Union’s 20th sanctions package against Russia and Belarus, but skips from some elements for now, the government said.
title: Switzerland Adopts Most of EU’s New Russia Sanctions Package

author: Jacob Reid
description: The Makerfield by-election is a high stakes gamble by Andy Burnham to wrestle power from Keir Starmer.
title: The 77,000 Voters Set to Decide the Next UK Prime Minister

author: Ellen Milligan
description: Huddled on a disused underground train platform in central London, hundreds of British soldiers played out their response to a fictional Russian attack on NATO, chewing through terabytes of data every day to direct fictional assets, including drones and robots, against the invasion.
title: NATO-Russia War Simulation Shows Risk of UK Defense Spending Gap

author: Sam Dagher, Zainab Fattah, Fiona MacDonald
description: The United Arab Emirates has made a more concerted push for an end to the Iran war in recent days, joining Saudi Arabia and Qatar in urging US President Donald Trump to give negotiations a chance, according to several people familiar with the matter.
title: UAE Joins Saudis, Qatar in Urging Trump Not to Restart Iran War

author: Patrick Sykes
description: The US and Iran have been locked in a stalemate since agreeing to a ceasefire in April. They’ve been unable to reach a deal to end a monthslong war that has killed thousands of people and sparked a global energy crunch.
title: The Key Sticking Points for a US-Iran Peace Deal

author: Jonathan Tamari
description: A month after an indefinite ceasefire, the endgame remains elusive
title: Costs Rise and Political Fallout Deepens Over Iran Stalemate

author: Patrick Sykes, Eric Martin
description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was “slight progress” in mediated negotiations with Iran, as the prospect of a deal to turn a fragile ceasefire into a lasting peace agreement remains uncertain.
title: US Touts ‘Slight Progress’ as Deal With Iran Remains in Limbo

author: Alberto Brambilla, Luca Casiraghi
description: Italy is set to extend its energy relief measures, with Industry Minister Adolfo Urso saying the support would remain in place as long as the Iran war pushes up fuel and energy prices for households and businesses.
title: Italy Set to Prolong Fuel Aid Even as Iran War Weighs on Economy

author: Tom Rees
description: A smile on his face, Keir Starmer approached reporters outside Downing Street on Thursday to talk up recent data that suggested that Britain was the fastest growing economy in the Group of Seven.
title: Britain’s Economy Turns Sour Just as Starmer Had a Reason to Brag

author: Enda Curran
description: Kevin Warsh, who’s promised the biggest shakeup in decades at the US central bank, is set to be sworn into office Friday in a White House ceremony as the 17th chair of the Federal Reserve.
title: Warsh to Be Sworn in as Fed Chief During White House Ceremony

author: Alex Wickham
description: Andy Burnham, the would-be successor to Keir Starmer as prime minister, pledged to change Britain’s economy as he launched a special election campaign that could clear his path to 10 Downing Street.
title: Burnham Vows to Change UK Economy in Official Campaign Launch

author: Gresa Kraja
description: Kosovo’s government approved cash handouts and higher maternity benefits 16 days before snap elections in which Prime Minister Albin Kurti is seeking re-election after months of political deadlock.
title: Kosovo Approves Cash Handouts 16 Days Ahead of Snap Elections

description: Trump wants to build the National Garden of Heroes, but he should instead look to the first Hall of Fame hidden on the beautiful campus of Bronx Community College, says Bloomberg Opinion columnist Frank Barry. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Should Revive This Hall Of Fame

author: Sergio Mendoza
description: Rodrigo Paz was elected with broad support to tackle an economic crisis. Now many just want him to go.
title: Bolivia’s New President Is In Trouble After Just Six Months

author: Alessandra Migliaccio, Georgios Georgiou, Jana Randow
description: The European Union is considering Italy’s plea to get more leeway on the bloc’s fiscal rules as the Iran war raises costs for households and businesses.
title: EU Reviewing Italy’s Call to Ease Fiscal Rules as Costs Rise

author: Grace Sihombing
description: Indonesia’s President Prabowo Subianto has been undertaking an ambitious agenda to try to remake Southeast Asia’s biggest economy. The centerpiece is an effort to lift annual growth to 8%, up from an average of roughly 5% over the past decade.
title: Why Prabowo’s Commodity Export Controls Are Spooking Indonesian Markets

author: Ott Tammik, Milda Seputyte
description: Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna accused Russia of “guiding” stray Ukrainian military drones toward NATO countries after a series of airspace incursions caused disruption in the Baltic states this week.
title: Russia Is ‘Guiding’ Drones Into NATO Airspace, Estonia Says

description: An attack on a nuclear power plant in the United Arab Emirates has raised fears about the scope of Iran’s retaliation to a potential US resumption of strikes, with experts highlighting the greater role Tehran-backed militias in Iraq are playing in the war. Meanwhile, the US and Iran are seeking to turn a fragile ceasefire into a more permanent end to fighting, but have yet to reach an agreement. Bloomberg's Abeer Abu Omar reports from Dubai. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US-Iran Talks Progress Undermined By Hormuz, Uranium Divide

author: Alaric Nightingale
description: Ukraine targeted the Yaroslavl oil refinery in central Russia overnight to inflict further damage on its foe’s energy infrastructure, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
title: Ukraine Says It Targeted Russia’s Yaroslavl Oil Refinery Again

author: Jim Wyss
description: Ever since US Special Forces captured Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro on Jan. 3 and launched an attack on Iran, Washington has been warning that Cuba will be next. Under a US-imposed economic blockade, the island has received almost no fuel in 2026. On May 13, Cuba’s energy minister said the country has completely run out of the diesel and fuel oil it needs to keep its power plants running.
title: Can Cuba’s Regime Survive Rising US Pressure?

author: Kamil Kowalcze
description: Germany plans to increase the firepower of its national raw-materials fund by as much as half to €1.5 billion ($1.7 billion) as it seeks to reduce dependence on critical supplies from countries such as China and shore up supply chains. Officials are also considering expanding the vehicle into a sovereign wealth fund from 2028 onward.
title: Germany to Boost Raw-Materials Fund to Reduce Reliance on China

author: Jana Randow, Alessandra Migliaccio, Georgios Georgiou
description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde stressed that long-term inflation expectations are still broadly in line with the 2% target, despite deepening fallout from the Iran war.
title: ECB Chief Says Inflation Expectations Remain On Target

author: Antony Sguazzin, Mathabiso Ralengau
description: On a Friday last November, government officials representing Lesotho, a mountainous enclave in eastern South Africa, sat down in the capital Maseru for three hours of negotiations with Trump administration counterparts.
title: Secretive Deals, Aggressive Demands Are New US Foreign Aid Tactics

description: Ifo President Clemens Fuest discusses Germany's business outlook as an expectations index by the institute rose to 83.8 in May from a revised 83.5 the previous month. "Businesses are trying to adapt to this new situation," he says. Speaking on Bloomberg Television, Fuest adds:  "We see lower growth in Germany, but we don't see a recession." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Ifo Sees 'Lower Growth,' But No Recession in Germany

description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer is a "dud," veteran political journalist David Dimbleby tells Mishal Husain.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: UK Leader Starmer Is a ‘Dud’ Dimbleby Says

author: David Herbling
description: Kenyan President William Ruto ruled out further cuts to fuel taxes, even after deadly protests over the high cost of diesel brought the nation’s capital to a standstill this week.
title: Kenyan President Rules Out Further Fuel-Tax Cuts After Protests

description: Tobias Adrian, the International Monetary Fund's Financial Counsellor and Monetary and Capital Markets Director, discusses the response by global economies to the supply shocks created by the Iran war as well as efforts to achieve a coordinated response to cyberattacks, as AI accelerates the threat. Adrian joined Lizzy Burden on Bloomberg Daybreak Europe. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: IMF Financial Counsellor on Global Economy, Cybersecurity

author: Ellen Milligan, Jorge Valero, Alex Wickham
description: The next UK-European Union summit may be postponed as negotiations to deepen ties falter and Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s authority weakens.
title: UK-EU Summit Risks Delay Over Slow Progress and Weakened Starmer

author: Sam Dagher
description: The attack on a nuclear power plant in the United Arab Emirates raised fears about the scope of Iran’s retaliation to a US resumption of strikes, with experts highlighting the greater role Iran-backed militias in Iraq are playing in the war.
title: Attack on UAE Nuclear Plant From Iraq ‘Warning Shot’ By Iran

author: Daniel Basteiro
description: The European Union has made little progress in talks with Anthropic PBC to get its banks and companies tested for digital vulnerabilities that the new Mythos AI model uncovers, Spain’s economy minister said.
title: EU-Anthropic Talks Over Mythos Concerns Are Stalled, Spain Says

author: Sachin Ravikumar
description: British police investigating former prince Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor over potential misconduct in public office are also assessing the possibility of sex crimes dating back to 2010.
title: Probe Into Former Prince Andrew Assesses Potential Sex Crimes

author: Andrea Palasciano, Charlie Duxbury
description: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte welcomed an abrupt announcement by President Donald Trump to send an additional 5,000 troops to Poland even as the alliance’s top envoys braced for cuts in US military resources.
title: NATO Welcomes New Trump Troop Pledge as Allies Caught Off Guard

author: William Horobin
description: French business confidence remained weak in May, adding to evidence that the fallout from the Iran war is weighing on domestic demand in the euro area’s second-largest economy.
title: French Business Confidence Languishes Below Long-Term Average

author: Tom Rees
description: UK government borrowing hit the highest level for any April in six years, as pressure on the public finances mounts from the Iran war and political instability at home.
title: UK Posts Highest April Budget Deficit Since the Pandemic

author: Daniel Basteiro, Alessandra Migliaccio, Kamil Kowalcze
description: European Union economy chief Valdis Dombrovskis said the European Central Bank will need to address the continent’s rising inflation due to the war in Iran.
title: EU’s Dombrovskis Sees ECB Rate Response to Inflation Shock

author: Helen Nyambura
description: The US sanctioned a Tanzanian police chief over the alleged torture of detained human-rights activists in the lead-up to last year’s disputed presidential elections.
title: US Sanctions Tanzanian Police Chief Over Alleged Rights Abuses

description: A Turkish court removed the leader of the country’s main opposition party, the Republican People’s Party (CHP), in a landmark ruling that led to a stock market selloff and state intervention to defend the lira. The court decision voids the election of Ozgur Ozel as CHP chairman. Bloomberg's Beril Akman reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Turkish Court Unseats Leader of Main Opposition Party

author: Jennifer Duggan
description: Ireland is about to get another lesson in how quickly its political landscape is shifting in two elections on Friday on opposite sides of the country.
title: Irish Elections to Showcase Voter Anger After Fuel Protests

description: US President Donald Trump said he opposed efforts by Iran and Oman to establish some form of permanent toll system through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran said the latest US proposal partly bridged the gap between the warring sides, but comments from the Islamic Republic’s supreme leader about keeping Tehran’s uranium stockpile and a dispute over tolls in the key waterway clouded the outlook for a breakthrough. Bloomberg's Stuart Livingstone-Wallace reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Talks Progress Undercut by Hormuz, Uranium Divide

description: David Dimbleby anchored BBC coverage of 10 UK general elections. With Prime Minister Keir Starmer under pressure, he is uniquely placed to understand the characters shaping British politics today. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: David Dimbleby: The UK Is in a Dire State

author: Misha Savic, Jan Bratanic, Andrea Dudik
description: If the European Union has a red line in Serbia’s relationship to China, President Aleksandar Vucic may be getting close.
title: Chinese Missiles and Robots Find Warm Welcome in EU’s Backyard

author: Volodymyr Verbianyi
description: Ukraine and its allies are increasingly confident that Russia’s invasion is running out of steam as Kyiv stabilizes the front line and stalls a spring offensive by Moscow.
title: Ukraine and Allies Grow Confident Russia’s Invasion Losing Steam

author: Rong Wei Neo
description: Singapore shipping tycoon Teo Siong Seng was accused by the US of colluding to raise dry-container prices, placing one of the city-state’s most prominent business figures at the center of a sweeping antitrust case.
title: Singapore Shipping Magnate Accused by US in Price Fixing Scheme

author: Colum Murphy, Lucille Liu, Yoshiaki Nohara
description: China called for Asia-Pacific economies to deepen cooperation in the face of global tensions, as some of Beijing’s trading partners plan tougher measures to address their growing trade imbalance with the manufacturing powerhouse.
title: China Rallies Asia-Pacific Against Protectionism at Trade Meet

author: Yoshiaki Nohara
description: Japanese Trade Minister Ryosei Akazawa said it would be natural to seek communication with his Chinese counterpart Wang Wentao when they both attend an international conference starting Friday, as Tokyo aims to engage with China amid strained ties.
title: Japan Says Natural to Seek Communication With China At APEC

author: Iain Boekhoff
description: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said she’ll call a referendum on whether the energy-rich province should stay in Canada or start a legal process that could eventually lead to its independence.
title: Alberta Premier Calls Vote on Oil-Rich Region’s Future in Canada

author: Alex Vasquez
description: Mexico’s ruling party is proposing a reform to annul future elections if there’s interference by foreign individuals, organizations or governments seeking to influence the results.
title: Mexico Lawmaker Pitches Voiding Elections If Foreigners Meddle

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, John Bolton, former National Security Advisor in President Trump's first term, says negotiations with Iran will not produce a satisfactory deal, and Jovita Neliupšienė, Ambassador of the European Union to the United States, says Europe supports freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz as higher energy prices pressure European economies. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Senate Will Leave For Recess Without Budget Vote | Balance of Power: Late Edition 5/21/2026
